title.narrative: Strengthened flexible and inclusive apprenticeship programmes

description.narrative:
The intervention supports national efforts in Iraq to strengthen labour market governance, inclusive employment policies, and skills systems to improve access to decent work, particularly for youth, women, forcibly displaced persons, and host communities. Through technical cooperation and policy dialogue, the ILO supports the development and operationalization of the National Employment Policy, the strengthening of employment services and career guidance systems, and the expansion of inclusive apprenticeship, work-based learning, and vocational education and training (TVET) opportunities aligned with labour market needs.
The intervention also supports the institutionalization and expansion of Job Search Clubs (JSCs) within national systems to facilitate youth transitions into employment and formalization. In parallel, the intervention contributes to strengthening labour governance and rights at work by supporting national efforts to prevent and address violence and harassment in the world of work in line with Convention No. 190 and Recommendation No. 206. This includes support for the review of labour legislation, development of workplace codes of conduct and prevention tools, and awareness-raising and institutional coordination efforts to promote safer, more inclusive, and rights-based working environments.
Through integrated policy support, institutional strengthening, and collaboration with government institutions, social partners, and other stakeholders, the intervention aims to improve employability, strengthen labour market inclusion, promote decent work transitions, and reinforce inclusive and resilient labour market systems in Iraq.
